Monday, August 24 was a rough session for Jaleel's book, with the bulk of the damage concentrated in the higher-conviction tech and growth names. NVDA fell 2.91% — the market pulling back ahead of its Q2 earnings report due Wednesday, August 26 — while BSX shed 2.7% and AVGO dropped 2.63%, the latter hit by overlapping concerns around AI-capex sentiment and Fed minutes signaling that higher rates may still be on the table. RKLB was the session's worst performer, off 5.91%, compounding an already painful unrealized loss of 12.9%; that position carries an AVOID verdict and the weakest QARP score in the book at 38.3, making it the sharpest divergence between where the thesis has landed and where the price is going. On the other side, AZO added 1.74% and LULU gained 1.41%, while ADBE and SAP both edged higher after B of A lifted price targets across software on easing AI-disruption fears — a modest but welcome narrative shift for ADBE given its persistent sentiment headwind.

The drift to watch is BSX: down 2.7% today, essentially flat on the unrealized gain (0.0%), yet still rated STRONG BUY with a QARP of 75.8. That's a textbook case of price and thesis pulling in opposite directions — management already guided flat through Q3 after slashing FY26 growth expectations, and the next catalyst isn't until October 20. The book's overall unrealized gain sits at 4.31%, but with nearly 27% of weight in names that are underwater (ZTS, RKLB, LULU, ONON, AVGO, NVS) and a semiconductor complex bracing for a binary event Wednesday, that cushion is thinner than it looks.

The NVDA earnings print on August 26 is the single most consequential near-term event — it touches not just the 9% NVDA weight directly but sets the tone for AVGO and broader AI-capex sentiment. The drug-pricing overhang (MFN deals, tariffs) continues to hang quietly over the pharma cluster — GILD, NVS, NBIX, and VRTX combined represent a modest slice of the book, but policy risk there is real and ongoing. RKLB remains the position most in need of a hard re-examination.

attention.headline: Q2 earnings Wednesday Aug 26 — binary event with export-control overhang
attention.note: At 9% weight, down 2.91% today on pre-earnings jitters and ongoing China export-license tightening, the Wednesday print will either validate the STRONG BUY thesis or accelerate the pullback — Jaleel's book needs a clear stance on sizing before the report drops.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated position down 5.91% today, -12.9% unrealized — thesis has broken
attention.note: With the lowest QARP in the book at 38.3 and an explicit AVOID verdict, today's 5.91% drop makes continued holding a decision in itself; the gap between the system's rating and the current position needs to be resolved.

attention.headline: STRONG BUY vs. flat unrealized gain and slashed guidance — drift widening
attention.note: Down 2.7% today and essentially breakeven on the position despite a 9.3% weight, BSX's price action is increasingly disconnected from the STRONG BUY rating, and with management guiding flat through Q3 and the next catalyst not until October 20, the risk is that the thesis re-rating comes too late.

attention.headline: B of A target raise helps sentiment, but CFO exit and AI-moat fear persist into Sep 10 earnings
attention.note: Today's software tailwind is real but the underlying narrative risk — AI disruption, CFO departure, ARR de-emphasis — hasn't resolved, and September 10 earnings will be the next moment of truth for whether the re-rating sticks.
